Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 32,844 plants/acre (97% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 97% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Spatial distribution:
    - adequate: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Species: Volunteer corn (V6-V12), Pigweeds (R2-R4)
  Description: Weed pressure was none at Mission 1 (VE-V1), remained none through Mission 2, remained none through Mission 3, escalated to mild at Mission 4 (V6-V12), declined to none at Mission 5 (V13-V16), escalated to mild at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition. Favorable moisture following 3.4 in of rain between May 13 and May 21 may have supported additional weed germination.
  Spatial distribution:
    - mild pressure: none pressure early, mild pressure late — Weed pressure was observed across the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  First detected: Not detected in-field
  Type: None detected in-field
  Regional context: Gray Leaf Spot was detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but was not detected in this field.
  Description: No impact diseases were detected in-field across any late-season flight. Despite regional detections of Gray Leaf Spot in nearby fields during the R2-R4 window, your field remained free of these diseases, and the canopy stayed fully intact all season.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: low pressure — no impact diseases detected across the field.
  Yield impact: no — canopy integrity was maintained throughout the season.

Nutrients — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Recurring / Intermittent
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 2
  Type: Nitrogen, Deficiency - Other, Sulfur
  Description: Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at Mission 2, with 3.7% detections in the field, peaked at 18.2%, and decreased to 15% by R2-R4. Deficiency - Other deficiency was detected once, at Mission 4, with 4.3% at V6-V12. Sulfur deficiency was first detected at Mission 5, with 13.6% at V13-V16, and appeared following heavy rainfall (6.9 in between Jun 10 and Jun 29), suggesting nutrient leaching may have contributed to the observed deficiency.
  Spatial distribution:
    - scattered: Moderate deficiency — Other and Nitrogen deficiencies are scattered around the field, not concentrated in any particular region(s).
  Yield impact: yes — some yield drag is plausible but not confirmed significant.

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  Description: No insect pressure was detected at any point during the season.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - 4 day(s) of frost risk (Apr 19–May 3) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - 1 day(s) of frost risk (May 3) occurred during the Mission 1 → Mission 2 window.
  - Heavy precipitation events (May 27 (2.3 in), Jun 10 (2.3 in)) occurred during the Mission 3 → Mission 4 window.
  - Multiple heavy precipitation events (Jun 10 (2.3 in)) during the Mission 4 → Mission 5 window increased the risk of nutrient leaching and delivery challenges, particularly for Sulfur.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 11 days within Apr 18–May 3; 5 days within May 3–May 9; 5 days within May 15–May 21; 10 days within May 21–Jun 10; 9 days within Jun 10–Jun 28; 8 days within Jun 30–Jul 17, but no impact diseases developed in-field.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.
summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Moderate nutrient deficiencies likely had a moderate impact on yield potential, while strong emergence and effective weed control kept other threats to a minor factor.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 97% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was absent early, declined to none at V13–V16, and returned to mild at R2–R4; likely negligible yield impact.

High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 11 days within Apr 18–May 3; 5 days within May 3–May 9; 5 days within May 15–May 21; 10 days within May 21–Jun 10; 9 days within Jun 10–Jun 28; 8 days within Jun 30–Jul 17, but no impact diseases developed in-field. No impact diseases were detected in-field, and the canopy remained fully intact throughout the season, likely negligible yield impact.

Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at V4–V5 (3.7% detections in the field), peaked at 18.2%, and decreased to 15% by R2–R4. Deficiency - Other was detected at V6–V12 (4.3%). Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V13–V16 (13.6%) following 6.9 in of rain between Jun 10 and Jun 29, with leaching a likely contributing factor; likely having a moderate yield impact.

No insect pressure was detected at any point during the season, likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 29,983 plants/acre (91% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 91% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V4-V5)
  Species: Pigweeds (V4-V5, V6-V12, V13-V16, VT-R1, R2-R4), Barnyard grass (V6-V12, V13-V16, VT-R1, R2-R4), Morning glory (V13-V16)
  Description: Weed pressure was mild at Mission 1 (V4-V5), remained mild through Mission 2 (V6-V12), escalated to moderate at Mission 3 (V13-V16), remained moderate through Mission 4 (VT-R1), escalated to high at Mission 5 (R2-R4), remained high through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure increased as the season progressed, suggesting continued weed emergence or declining residual control. Favorable moisture following 2.8 in of rain between Jun 1 and Jun 16 may have supported additional weed germination. Post-emergence timing needs review, given moderate or higher weed pressure detected after Mission 2.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: mild pressure early, high pressure late — Weed pressure was concentrated in localized pockets across the field, and weed pressure increased as the season progressed, suggesting continued weed emergence or declining residual control.
  Yield impact: no — pressure reached moderate or higher at points during the season, but the timing limited this season's yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Recurring / Intermittent
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 2 (V6-V12)
  Type: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight, Rust, Gray Leaf Spot, Tar Spot
  Non-impact detections: Anthracnose leaf blight: detected at V6-V12, Holcus Leaf Spot: detected at V6-V12, Downy mildew: detected at V13-V16
  Description: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was first detected in-field at Mission 2 (V6-V12), 0.8% detections in the field, peaked at 91.6%; still detected in-field at the final mission (Mission 6/6, 91.6%). Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was also detected regionally in up to 12 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Rust was first detected in-field at Mission 3 (V13-V16), 0.3%; no longer detected in-field by the final mission (Mission 6/6). Rust was also detected regionally in up to 1 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Gray Leaf Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 3 (V13-V16); present in-field but not significant at the final mission (Mission 6/6). Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 12 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Tar Spot was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4), 0.8% — a single data point, not a trajectory. Tar Spot was also detected regionally in up to 4 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Conditions between Apr 24 and Jun 1 were also conducive to disease spread.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Moderate pressure — disease was present in scattered pockets across the field, without a single dominant zone.
  Yield impact: yes — unresolved in-field disease pressure likely reduced canopy function during a yield-relevant window.

Nutrients — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Steady Medium
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 2 (Representative stage: V6-V12)

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Unresolved foliar disease during grain fill and persistent nutrient deficiencies likely had a moderate impact on yield potential, despite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 91% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was mild at V4–V5, escalated to moderate at V13–V16, and reached high levels at R2–R4, with pigweeds, barnyard grass, and morning glory concentrated in pockets; pressure increased as the season progressed, but likely negligible yield impact.

Northern Corn Leaf Blight was first detected at V6–V5 (0.8% detections in the field), peaked and increased to 91.6% at the final assessment; regional detections of NCLB occurred alongside in-field escalation. Rust was first detected at V13–V16 (0.3%), but was no longer detected by the final mission, with regional detections occurring at the same time. Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at V13–V16 and remained present but not significant at the final mission, with regional detections also observed concurrently. Tar Spot was detected once at R2–R4 (0.8%), with regional detections noted at the same time. Weather conditions were conducive to disease spread during this period. Anthracnose leaf blight, Holcus Leaf Spot and Downy mildew were detected but are considered low impact. Unresolved in-field disease pressure likely had a moderate yield impact.

Potassium deficiency was detected once at V6–V12 (4.9% detections in the field). Phosphorus deficiency was detected once at V6–V12 (3.2%). Magnesium deficiency was detected once at V13–V16 (0.5%). Sulfur deficiency was detected once at V13–V16 (5.1%). These deficiencies were scattered across the field and appeared transient, likely having a moderate yield impact.

Japanese beetle was detected at V13–V16 (0.3% detections in the field), increased to 0.4% at VT–R1, but was not detected by the final mission, consistent with management and within a non-critical window. Stink bug was detected during the season but not at the final mission, also within a non-critical window. Chewing damage and insect pressure were observed at low levels at VT–R1 and R2–R4, but overall insect pressure was likely negligible in terms of yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Moderate weed pressure at V4–V5 unresolved foliar during grain fill likely had a moderate impact on yield potentialdespite a strong final stand.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 93% of target, indicating strong emergence.

Weed pressure was moderate at V4–V5, escalated to high at V6–V12, reached very high at V6–V12, remained very high from V6–V12 through VT–R1, declined to high at R2–R4, and escalated to very high at R2–R4; pigweeds, barnyard grass, velvetleaf, and broadleaf species were dominant, with pressure increasing as the season progressed and favorable moisture following 2.1 in of rain on May 16 likely supporting additional weed germination — likely having a moderate yield impact.

Northern Corn Leaf Blight was first detected at V6–V12 (0.1% detections in the field), peaked at 28.3%, and was still present at 28.3% at the final assessment; Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at VT–R1 and remained present but not significant at the final mission; Tar Spot was detected once at R2–R4 (0.4%) after regional detections earlier in the season; conditions lent themselves to disease pressure during this period. Rust was present regionally but not detected in this field. Anthracnose leaf blight, Downy mildew and Holcus Leaf Spot were detected but are considered low impact. Unresolved in-field disease pressure likely had a negligible yield impact.

Potassium deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (0.1% detections in the field), peaked at 0.4%, and decreased to 0.1% by R2–R4, concentrated in about 20% of the field. Magnesium deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (0.8%), decreased to 0.4% by VT–R1, and was no longer detected by the final mission, also concentrated in about 20% of the field. Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (5.7%), decreasing to 0.4% by R2–R4. Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (0.1%), peaking at 10.3%. Phosphorus deficiency was detected once at R2–R4 (0.1%). Persistent deficiencies in potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus were noted, but overall nutrient impact was likely negligible.

Japanese beetle was first detected at V6–V12 (1.6% detections in the field), increased to 20.7% at V6–V12, declined to 0.3% at VT–R1, and was not detected by the final mission, with pressure within the critical window likely having a significant yield impact. Stink bug and European corn borer were detected during the season but not at the final mission, with their respective critical windows after R4 and at V6–V8, respectively. Chewing damage was first detected at V6–V12 (3.8%), increased to 13.4% at V6–V12, declined to 10.5% at VT–R1, and increased to 13.6% at R2–R4, with overall insect pressure remaining low and likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Moderate weed pressure at V13–V16 unresolved foliar during grain fill likely had a moderate impact on yield potentialdespite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 91% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was moderate at V0–VE, escalated to very high at V13–V16, and declined to moderate at R2–R4, with pigweeds, barnyard grass, and velvetleaf concentrated in pockets; pressure decreased only partially following treatment, and favorable moisture following 3.6 in of rain between May 31 and Jun 15 may have supported additional weed germination, likely having a moderate yield impact.

Northern Corn Leaf Blight was first detected at R2–R4 (0.7% detections in the field), with no in-field detection by the final assessment; Gray Leaf Spot was also first detected at R2–R4, peaking at 7.6% and still present at 7.6% at the final mission, with both diseases detected regionally before appearing in-field. Conditions lent themselves to disease pressure during this period. Rust and Tar Spot were present in nearby fields but not detected in this field. Unresolved in-field disease pressure likely had a negligible yield impact.

Magnesium deficiency was first detected at V4–V5 (1.4% detections in the field), peaking at 1.5% and concentrated in about 10% of the field. Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V4–V5 (2.2%), peaked at 9.3%, and decreased to 2.8% by R2–R4, with deficiency concentrated in about 10% of the field. Phosphorus deficiency was first detected at V4–V5 (0.7%), concentrated in about 10% of the field. Nitrogen deficiency was detected once at R2–R4 (4.6%), with deficiency concentrated in about 10% of the field. These deficiencies were transient or well within adequate range, likely negligible yield impact.

Chewing damage was first detected at R2–R4 (2.8% detections in the field), increased to 11.4% at R2–R4, and insect pressure was observed at 1.5% at R2–R4, but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: Any specific named threat (species, disease, deficiency) mentioned in the summary must appear in the analysis

Non-impact diseases detected in the season must be mentioned in the summary — group all non-impact diseases together in one brief clause using "considered low impact" phrasing (e.g., "downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact" — never "was also detected"; "also" has nothing to point at and is faulted even when a prior disease is in scope). A clause that states the same thing in its own words ("did not reach impactful thresholds", "low-impact") satisfies this — the mandated wording is not owed on top of it. No trajectory language, no yield language, no further detail. If no non-impact diseases were detected, this criterion is not applicable.

A growth-stage token cited anywhere in the summary must match some mission's actual (Representative, or clearly-dominant) stage reading in season_data -- never a stage no mission recorded. Dominant pattern (c) from the original annotator review: a fabricated stage citation, distinct from the trend-language checks above. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

summary_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 31,336 plants/acre (101% of target)
  Uniformity: Good (CV 36.7%)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 101% of target and with low variability (CV 36.7%). Strong emergence and establishment.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → Middle Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: VE-V1)
  Species: Pigweeds (V3-V4, V6-V12, V13-V16, VT-R1), Barnyard grass (V6-V12, VT-R1, R2-R4), Volunteer corn (VE-V1)
  Description: Weed pressure was mild at Mission 1 (VE-V1), escalated to very high at Mission 2 (V3-V4), declined to mild at Mission 3 (V6-V12), remained mild through Mission 4 (V13-V16), remained mild through Mission 5 (VT-R1), remained mild through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Early weed pressure suggests pre-emergence control was incomplete, but later applications effectively reduced competition. Favorable moisture following 2.9 in of rain on May 16 may have supported additional weed germination.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: mild pressure throughout — Weed pressure was concentrated in localized pockets across the field, and early weed pressure suggests pre-emergence control was incomplete, but later applications effectively reduced competition.
  Yield impact: yes — some competitive drag on yield is plausible but not confirmed significant.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → Middle Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (V13-V16)
  Type: Gray Leaf Spot, Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight
  Description: Gray Leaf Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 4 (V13-V16), 3.1% detections in the field; no longer detected in-field by the final mission (Mission 6/6). Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 11 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4), 0.4% — a single data point, not a trajectory. Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was also detected regionally in up to 15 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, before it was detected in-field. Conditions between May 9 and May 23 were also conducive to disease spread. Rust was detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but was not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — Disease detections were concentrated in localized pockets across the field, concentrated in about 9.9% of the total area.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Persistent potassium and sulfur deficiencies likely had a significant impact on yield potential, while moderate weed pressure and unresolved stink bug activity at the critical reproductive window likely had a moderate yield impact.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 101% detections in the field of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was mild at VE-V1, escalated to very high at V3-V4, then declined to mild and remained mild through the rest of the season; pigweeds, barnyard grass, and volunteer corn were dominant, with pressure concentrated in localized pockets and favorable moisture following 2.9 in of rain on May 16 likely supporting additional weed germination — likely having a moderate yield impact.

Potassium deficiency was first detected at V6-V12 (0.8% detections in the field), concentrated in about 7% of the field, and was no longer detected by the final mission. Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at V6-V12 (0.4%), peaking at 8.6%, and sulfur deficiency was detected once at V13-V16 (38.5%) — persistent deficiencies likely had a significant yield impact.

Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at V13-V16 (3.1% detections in the field), with no in-field detection by the final mission, and was detected regionally alongside in-field detection in up to 11 fields. NCLB was detected once at R2-R4 (0.4%), with regional presence in up to 15 fields before in-field detection. Conditions between May 9 and May 23 were also conducive to disease spread. Rust was present in up to 1 field regionally but was not detected in this field — likely negligible yield impact.

Japanese beetle was first detected at V13-V16 (0.8% detections in the field), not detected by the final mission, and was outside the pollination window. Stink bug was detected at R2-R4 (0.4%) and remained present at the final mission, with feeding within the kernel set window. European corn borer was detected during the season but not at the final mission, with whorl feeding at V6–V8. Chewing damage increased to 13.5% at VT-R1, grasshopper and insect pressure were each detected at low levels at R2-R4, and overall insect pressure remained low — likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A growth-stage token cited anywhere in the summary must match some mission's actual (Representative, or clearly-dominant) stage reading in season_data -- never a stage no mission recorded. Season Conclusion must include exactly the threat categories whose Final_Yield_Impact (past + future bu/ac loss from the final mission, from the YIELD IMPACT DATA block) crosses the crop-specific threshold — corn: 5 bu/ac, soy: 3 bu/ac — and must omit any category that does not cross it

The weed block's last stage-bound pressure claim must not be superseded by a mission the narrative never reaches. Field 1312426 says "remained moderate through V13-V16" of a record whose sixth and final mission records Pressure: high at R2-R4 — every clause true, and the season reported as ending moderate when it ended high. Neighbour to SEASON_SUMMARY_WEED_TREND_GROUNDED, which asks whether a resolution or decrease claim is CONTRADICTED by the final mission; a block that fails that one is not graded here, so one sentence is never two criteria's 0. Span claims ("remained high throughout the season") bind to no mission and reach the end by construction, so they are out of scope.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Persistent very high weed pressure likely had a significant impact on yield potential, while other threats were negligible or well controlled.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 98% detections in the field of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was very high from V1–V2 and persisted through V5–V6, with pigweeds, barnyard grass, and broadleaf species widespread and concentrated in localized pockets, likely having a significant yield impact.

Conditions between May 1 and May 29 were also conducive to disease spread. Brown Stem Rot/Sudden Death Syndrome was detected once at V5–V6 (1.1% detections in the field), concentrated in a single hotspot, but likely negligible yield impact.

Potassium deficiency was first detected at V3–V4 (0.5% detections in the field), concentrated in about 3% of the field. Nitrogen deficiency was also first detected at V3–V4 (0.5%), appearing following 2 in of rain on Jun 3, with leaching a likely contributing factor; both deficiencies were transient and likely negligible yield impact.

Defoliation was first detected at V3–V4 (0.1% detections in the field), increased to 0.4% at V5–V6, but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

**Season Conclusion:**
Suboptimal and uneven emergence, recurring and intermittent weed pressure, and persistent nutrient deficiencies likely had a moderate impact on yield potential, despite a managed disease and insect situation.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 84% of target, with high variability (CV 49.1%), indicating suboptimal and uneven emergence despite favorable weather, which set a lower yield ceiling for the season.

Weed pressure was moderate at VE-V1, remained moderate through V1-V2 and V5-V6, escalated to high at V13-V16, declined to mild at VT-R1, and escalated again to moderate at R2-R4; pigweeds, barnyard grass, velvetleaf, and broadleaf species were dominant, with pressure concentrated in pockets and only partial control achieved following 3.6 in of rain on Jun 4, likely having a moderate yield impact.

Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at VT-R1 (0.7% detections in the field), present but not significant at the final assessment; conditions lent themselves to disease pressure during this period. NCLB and Tar Spot were present regionally but not detected in this field. Downy mildew, Holcus Leaf Spot and Anthracnose leaf blight were detected but are considered low impact. Disease pressure was limited and likely negligible yield impact.

Phosphorus deficiency was first detected at V5-V6 (0.2% detections in the field), potassium deficiency at V13-V16 (1.2%), and sulfur and nitrogen deficiencies at V13-V16 (1.0% and 1%, respectively), with all deficiencies concentrated in about 2% of the field and likely having a moderate yield impact.

Japanese beetle and stink bug were detected at V13-V16 and R2-R4, respectively, with Japanese beetle still present at the final mission within the critical silk clipping window, and stink bug remaining at R2-R4 within its critical window; chewing damage and grasshopper were also observed at low levels, but overall insect pressure was low and likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
No significant yield impact identified this season — strong emergence and in-season management kept all threats to a minor factor.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 100% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was mild at V1–V2, remained mild through V5–V6 and V6–V12, and was no longer detected by R2–R4; pigweeds, morning glory, and velvetleaf were present in localized pockets, with pressure developing primarily later in the season and likely negligible yield impact.

Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally alongside in-field detection. NCLB was present in up to 9 fields regionally but was not detected in this field. Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at R2–R4 (5.2% detections in the field), with no in-field detection by the final assessment; conditions lent themselves to disease spread during this period, but overall impact was likely negligible.

Potassium deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (0.7% detections in the field), concentrated in about 5% of the field. Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (0.3%), peaked at 1.7%, and was no longer detected by the final mission. Nitrogen deficiency was detected once at R2–R4 (0.3%). All deficiencies were transient or well within adequate range, likely negligible yield impact.

Stink bug was detected at V5–V6 (0.3% detections in the field), with critical window after R4, and chewing damage was observed at V13–V16 (3.8%), declining to 0.9% at R2–R4; overall insect pressure remained low, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

A weed-pressure severity, peak or first-detection claim tied to a growth stage must match the Pressure label the mission at that stage actually recorded. Per the requirements doc SS Content-Weeds the engine validates OVERALL pressure, not per-species trajectories (which the doc forbids the output from containing at all).

Season Conclusion must not assert a blanket "effective management" verdict for the whole season when the CATEGORY STATUS ground truth (copied into the analysis' Status: lines) shows any category as Unresolved. "Effective" is a definitive, unhedged claim of the same kind the Trajectory Language rules already ban for bare "Managed"/"Unmanaged" — hedged forms ("apparent effective management," "likely effective management," "appears to have been effectively managed") are acceptable.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Persistent very high weed pressure likely had a significant impact on yield potential, while other threats were negligible or well controlled.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 95% detections in the field of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was very high from V1–V2 through R5–R6, with pigweeds, barnyard grass, and fleabane/horseweed widespread and persistent throughout the season, likely having a significant yield impact.

Defoliation was first detected at V5–V6 (0.2% detections in the field), increased to 1.5% at R5–R6, but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 8 days within May 5–May 28; 5 days within Jun 20–Jun 26; 8 days within Jul 18–Aug 3; 11 days within Aug 3–Aug 20, but no impact diseases developed in-field. No impact diseases were detected in-field, and the canopy remained fully intact, likely negligible yield impact.

No nutrient deficiencies were detected at any point during the season, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

  Scenario: Steady High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V2-V3)
  Species: Pigweeds (V2-V3, V3-V4, V5-V6, R2-R4, R5-R6), Fleabane/Horseweed (V2-V3, V3-V4, V5-V6, R2-R4), Barnyard grass (V2-V3, V3-V4, V5-V6)
  Description: Weed pressure was very high at Mission 1 (V2-V3), remained very high through Mission 2 (V3-V4), remained very high through Mission 3 (V5-V6), declined to moderate at Mission 4 (R2-R4), remained moderate through Mission 5 (R2-R4), escalated to high at Mission 6 (R5-R6). Weed pressure decreased only partially following treatment, suggesting control was only partially effective. Reduced crop establishment may have increased crop-weed competition. Favorable moisture following 5.1 in of rain between Jul 21 and Aug 8 may have supported additional weed germination. Post-emergence timing needs review, given moderate or higher weed pressure detected after Mission 2.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: very high pressure early, high pressure late — Early-season weed pressure was widespread across the field, and weed pressure decreased only partially following treatment, suggesting control was only partially effective.
  Yield impact: no — pressure reached moderate or higher at points during the season, but the timing limited this season's yield risk.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Suboptimal but uniform emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season, while in-season threats were negligible and did not materially impact yield.

**Season Detail:**
Weather conditions were generally favorable, so non-weather factors may have contributed to the reduced stand.

Weed pressure was very high at V2–V3, remained very high through V5–V6, declined to moderate at R2–R4, remained moderate through R2–R4, and escalated to high at R5–R6; pressure decreased only partially following treatment, with pigweeds, fleabane/horseweed, and barnyard grass widespread and likely negligible yield impact.

Downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact. Brown Spot was first detected at R2–R4 (2.2% detections in the field), still present at 2.1% at final assessment, with Sudden Death Syndrome no longer detected by final mission; conditions lent themselves to disease pressure, but overall impact was likely negligible.

Defoliation was first detected at V3–V4 (0.3% detections in the field), increased to 1.3% at R5–R6, but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

No nutrient deficiencies were detected at any point during the season, likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Unresolved Brown Spot during grain fill and persistent magnesium and nitrogen deficiencies, along with disease pressure, likely had a significant impact on yield potential, despite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 96% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was mild at V3–V4, escalated to moderate at R5–R6, and reached high at R5–R6, with barnyard grass, velvetleaf, and common lambsquarters concentrated in pockets across the field; favorable moisture following 2.5 in of rain between Apr 29 and Jun 6 may have supported additional weed germination, but overall weed impact was likely negligible yield impact.

Downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact. Brown Spot was detected once at R5–R6 (38.5% detections in the field), with conditions conducive to disease spread present during this period, while Brown Stem Rot/Sudden Death Syndrome was first detected at R5–R6 (89.7%) and still present at 81.9% at the final assessment; both remained unresolved by season end, likely having a significant yield impact.

Magnesium deficiency was first detected at R2–R4 (12.8% detections in the field), peaked at 34.6%, and was no longer detected by the final mission. Potassium deficiency was detected once at R5–R6 (3.2%). Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at R5–R6 (76.9%), peaking at 100%, and appeared following heavy rainfall (2.5 in between Jul 21 and Aug 11), with persistent deficiency likely having a moderate yield impact.

Defoliation was first detected at V3–V4 (0.3% detections in the field), declined to 0.2% at V5–V6, remained at 0.2% at R2–R4, increased to 0.4% at R5–R6, and remained at 0.4% at R5–R6; insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: When S or N deficiency is described in the summary and a significant rainfall event occurred in the same window: if deficiency first appeared after the rain, the summary must write "appeared following heavy rainfall"; if deficiency was already present before the rain, the summary must write "intensified following heavy rainfall" — framing a pre-existing deficiency as having appeared post-rain scores 0.

A precipitation total cited for a specific date range (e.g. "2.2 in of rain between Jun 28-Jul 15") must be that window's own total in season_data -- not another window's figure reused against the wrong dates.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Persistent very high weed pressure likely had a significant impact on yield potential, while in-field threats were generally well controlled.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 94% detections in the field of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was very high from V2–V3 through R2–R4, with pigweeds, barnyard grass, and morning glory widespread and persistent throughout the season, likely having a significant yield impact.

Gray Leaf Spot was present in nearby fields regionally but not detected in this field. Holcus Leaf Spot was detected but is considered low impact. Northern Corn Leaf Blight was detected once at R2–R4 (0.8% detections in the field), with conditions conducive to disease spread present during this period, but overall impact was likely negligible.

Sulfur deficiency was detected once at V6–V12 (39.1% detections in the field), scattered around the field, likely negligible yield impact.

Japanese beetle was first detected at V6–V12 (0.9% detections in the field) and was not detected by the final mission, consistent with management and outside the pollination window. Chewing damage was also observed at 8.6% at R2–R4, but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Poor emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season, with sustained high weed pressure likely having a significant yield impact.

**Season Detail:**
Weather conditions were generally favorable, so a broad management, seeding, or field-level issue may explain the low stand.

Weed pressure was very high from VC-V1 through V5-V6, with pigweeds, barnyard grass, and fleabane/horseweed present in widespread, persistent pockets across the field, likely having a significant yield impact.

High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 6 days within Jun 20–Jun 26, but no impact diseases developed in-field. No impact diseases were detected in-field or regionally at any point during the season, likely negligible yield impact.

No nutrient deficiencies were detected at any point during the season, likely negligible yield impact.

Defoliation was detected at V13-V16 (0.5% detections in the field), but remained unresolved and critical window was outside flowering, likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Moderate weed pressure at V2–V3 and escalating through the season likely had a moderate impact on yield potential, despite a strong final stand.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 92% of target, indicating strong emergence.

Weed pressure was moderate at VE, remained moderate through V0-VE, declined to mild at V5-V6, remained mild through V13-V16, escalated to moderate at R2-R4, and reached high at R2-R4, with pressure concentrated in localized pockets and increasing as the season progressed; 7.5 in of rain between Jun 13 and Jul 5 likely supported additional weed germination, likely having a moderate yield impact.

Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V5-V6 (2.1% detections in the field), and magnesium deficiency was first detected at V13-V16 (0.5%), both transient and concentrated in small pockets, likely negligible yield impact.

Stink bug was detected at R2-R4 (0.5% detections in the field) within the critical window, and chewing damage was observed at V5-V6 (0.5%), V13-V16 (1.6%), and R2-R4 (5.2% and 6.5%), but overall insect pressure remained low, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: Non-impact diseases detected in the season must be mentioned in the summary — group all non-impact diseases together in one brief clause using "considered low impact" phrasing (e.g., "downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact" — never "was also detected"; "also" has nothing to point at and is faulted even when a prior disease is in scope). A clause that states the same thing in its own words ("did not reach impactful thresholds", "low-impact") satisfies this — the mandated wording is not owed on top of it. No trajectory language, no yield language, no further detail. If no non-impact diseases were detected, this criterion is not applicable.

A growth-stage token cited anywhere in the summary must match some mission's actual (Representative, or clearly-dominant) stage reading in season_data -- never a stage no mission recorded. Dominant pattern (c) from the original annotator review: a fabricated stage citation, distinct from the trend-language checks above. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

C9 — a nutrient recorded at three or more missions with a genuinely moving series must not be reported as a single point reading. The sentence satisfies this with a second percentage of its own or with a trend/resolution word; no specific phrasing is required. 1312426: potassium reads 1.9%% -> 4.9%% -> 0.9%% and the summary reported only "4.9%% at V13-V16", erasing both the rise and the decline.
Each detected threat category name (or alias) appears somewhere in the summary text

summary_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Poor Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 108,787 plants/acre (66% of target)
  Description: Stand count was 66% of target. Poor but uniform emergence. Weather stress likely contributed to broad stand reduction. This is consistent with 2 day(s) of frost risk (Apr 29–May 2).
  Yield impact: yes — poor emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season.

Weeds — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Steady High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: VC-V1)
  Species: Pigweeds (VC-V1, V1-V2, V4-V5, V5-V6, R2-R4), Fleabane/Horseweed (VC-V1, V1-V2, V5-V6), Velvetleaf (V1-V2, V4-V5)
  Description: Weed pressure was moderate at Mission 1 (VC-V1), escalated to high at Mission 2 (V1-V2), remained high through Mission 3, escalated to very high at Mission 4 (V4-V5), declined to high at Mission 5 (V5-V6), declined to moderate at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure decreased only partially following treatment, suggesting control was only partially effective. Reduced crop establishment may have increased crop-weed competition. Favorable moisture following 2.9 in of rain on May 16 may have supported additional weed germination. Post-emergence timing needs review, given moderate or higher weed pressure detected after Mission 2.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: moderate pressure throughout — Early-season weed pressure was widespread across the field, and weed pressure decreased only partially following treatment, suggesting control was only partially effective.
  Yield impact: no — pressure reached moderate or higher at points during the season, but the timing limited this season's yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → Middle Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 5 (V5-V6)
  Type: Brown Spot
  Non-impact detections: Downy mildew (Soybean): 4% at V5-V6
  Description: Brown Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 5 (V5-V6), 0.5% detections in the field; no longer detected in-field by the final mission (Mission 6/6). Conditions between Apr 23 and May 24 were also conducive to disease spread.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — Disease detections were concentrated in localized pockets across the field, concentrated in about 6.4% of the total area.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 5 (Representative stage: V5-V6)
  Type: Nitrogen, Magnesium
  Description: Nitrogen deficiency was detected once, at Mission 5, with 0.2% detections in the field at V5-V6. Magnesium deficiency was first detected at Mission 6, with 0.2% at R2-R4, concentrated in about 2% of the field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 2% of the field.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3
  Type: Defoliation
  Species status:
    Defoliation: Unresolved (still present at the final mission), Critical window: within R1–R3 (canopy loss during flowering and pod set)
  Description: Defoliation was first detected at Mission 3 at 0.2% detections in the field, remained at 0.2% at Mission 4 (V4-V5), increased to 0.3% at Mission 5 (V5-V6), declined to 0.2% at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Critical window: within R1–R3 (canopy loss during flowering and pod set). Status: Unresolved (still present at the final mission). Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Heavy precipitation events (May 16 (2.9 in)) between planting and Mission 1 likely contributed to soil compaction and emergence challenges.
  - 2 day(s) of frost risk (Apr 29–May 2) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 15 days within Apr 25–May 22; 9 days within Jun 12–Jun 27; 7 days within Jul 18–Aug 6, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Poor emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season, with no significant yield impact from weeds, disease, nutrients, or insects.

**Season Detail:**
Weather stress likely contributed to broad stand reduction, consistent with 2 days of frost risk within Apr 29–May 2.

Weed pressure was moderate at VC-V1, escalated to high at V1-V2, remained high through V4-V5, reached very high at V4-V5, declined to high at V5-V6, and moderated to moderate at R2-R4; pressure decreased only partially following treatment, with pigweeds, fleabane/horseweed, and velvetleaf concentrated in pockets, but likely negligible yield impact.

Conditions between Apr 23 and May 24 were also conducive to disease spread. Downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact. Brown Spot was first detected at V5-V6 (0.5% detections in the field), and was no longer detected by the final mission, while Brown Stem Rot/Sudden Death Syndrome was also first detected at V5-V6 (0.5%), and no longer detected by the final mission; disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained, likely negligible yield impact.

Nitrogen deficiency was detected once at V5-V6 (0.2% detections in the field), and magnesium deficiency was first detected at R2-R4 (0.2%), both concentrated in small pockets, likely negligible yield impact.

Defoliation was first detected at V3-V4 (0.2% detections in the field), remained at 0.2% at V4-V5, increased slightly to 0.3% at V5-V6, and declined to 0.2% at R2-R4; insect pressure remained low, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A weed-pressure severity, peak or first-detection claim tied to a growth stage must match the Pressure label the mission at that stage actually recorded. Per the requirements doc SS Content-Weeds the engine validates OVERALL pressure, not per-species trajectories (which the doc forbids the output from containing at all).

A growth-stage token cited anywhere in the summary must match some mission's actual (Representative, or clearly-dominant) stage reading in season_data -- never a stage no mission recorded. Dominant pattern (c) from the original annotator review: a fabricated stage citation, distinct from the trend-language checks above. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
No significant yield impact identified this season — strong emergence and in-season management kept all threats to a minor factor.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 93% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was moderate at VE-V1, declined to mild through the season, and was controlled by R2-R4; barnyard grass, velvetleaf, and common lambsquarters were present in localized pockets, but overall impact was likely negligible.

Northern Corn Leaf Blight was detected once at R2-R4 (2% detections in the field), concentrated in localized pockets, with conditions conducive to disease spread present during this period, but likely negligible yield impact.

Magnesium deficiency was first detected at VT-R1 (0.5% detections in the field), and sulfur deficiency was first detected at V4-V5 (2.1%), peaking at 3.2% and no longer detected by the final mission; both were transient and likely negligible yield impact.

Stink bug was detected at V1-V2 and not detected by the final mission, with its critical window after R4, likely negligible yield impact. Chewing damage increased to 19.4% detections in the field at V13-V16, grasshopper was observed at VT-R1 (0.5%), and chewing damage increased to 30.6% at R2-R4; overall insect pressure remained low, likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Suboptimal but uniform emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season, while in-season threats remained negligible.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 88% of target, indicating suboptimal but uniform emergence; weather conditions were generally favorable, so non-weather factors may have contributed to the reduced stand.

Weed pressure was mild at VE-V1, escalated to high at V2-V3 and remained high through V6-V12, then declined to moderate at V13-V16 and was no longer detected by R2-R4; pressure increased as the season progressed, with favorable moisture following 1.9 in of rain between Apr 23 and May 14 supporting additional weed germination, but overall yield impact was likely negligible.

Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at R2-R4 (2.9% detections in the field), with no longer detected by the final mission; conditions lent themselves to disease spread during this period, but Gray Leaf Spot was no longer detected by the final mission. Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally alongside in-field detection. Tar Spot and NCLB were present regionally but not detected in this field. Chewing damage and insect pressure were detected at low levels at R2-R4, but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.

Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V6-V12 (5.3% detections in the field) and was no longer detected by the final mission. Potassium deficiency was detected once at V13-V16 (5.3%). Both deficiencies were transient or well within adequate range, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: Any specific named threat (species, disease, deficiency) mentioned in the summary must appear in the analysis

A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

A weed-pressure severity, peak or first-detection claim tied to a growth stage must match the Pressure label the mission at that stage actually recorded. Per the requirements doc SS Content-Weeds the engine validates OVERALL pressure, not per-species trajectories (which the doc forbids the output from containing at all).

When a CATEGORY STATUS block was computed for this record (it reaches the judge in its own field, not inside the analysis text), each threat category's Season Detail block must carry a qualitative yield-impact phrase derived from that category's Materiality field — Negligible/None -> "likely negligible yield impact", Moderate -> "likely having a moderate yield impact", Significant -> "likely having a significant yield impact". Wording may vary but the qualifier word must match the category's Materiality; do not re-derive the qualifier from severity language. Binary: a summary that omits one category's phrase is not partly right about that category, and proportional credit would score it above CORRECTION_THRESHOLD where no correction can reach it.

Emergence — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Medium Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 132,936 plants/acre (81% of target)
  Description: Stand count was 81% of target. Suboptimal but uniform emergence. Weather stress may have broadly reduced establishment across the field. This is consistent with frost (below 35°F) on May 12.
  Spatial distribution:
    - below threshold: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: yes — sub-optimal emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season.

Weeds — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Steady High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Significant
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V1-V2)
  Species: Pigweeds (V1-V2, V4-V5, R1, R2-R4, R5-R6), Common Lambsquarters (V1-V2, V3-V4, V4-V5, R1, R5-R6), Barnyard grass (V3-V4, V4-V5, R2-R4)
  Description: Weed pressure was very high at Mission 1 (V1-V2), remained very high through Mission 2 (V3-V4), remained very high through Mission 3 (V4-V5), declined to moderate at Mission 4 (R1), escalated to very high at Mission 5 (R2-R4), declined to moderate at Mission 6 (R5-R6). Weed pressure decreased only partially following treatment, suggesting control was only partially effective. Reduced crop establishment may have increased crop-weed competition. Favorable moisture following 2.2 in of rain between Jun 28 and Jul 21 may have supported additional weed germination. Post-emergence timing needs review, given moderate or higher weed pressure detected after Mission 2.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: very high pressure early, moderate pressure late — Early-season weed pressure was widespread across the field, and weed pressure decreased only partially following treatment, suggesting control was only partially effective.
  Yield impact: yes — sustained or unresolved pressure likely reduced yield potential.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 6 (R5-R6)
  Type: Brown Stem Rot/Sudden Death Syndrome (Sds)
  Non-impact detections: Downy mildew (Soybean): 21.1% at R1
  Description: Brown Stem Rot/Sudden Death Syndrome (Sds) was detected once, at Mission 6 (R5-R6) — a single data point, not a trajectory. Conditions between May 8 and Jun 8 were also conducive to disease spread. Brown Stem Rot was detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but was not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — disease was present in scattered pockets across the field, without a single dominant zone.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  Type: none
  Description: No nutrient deficiencies were detected at any point during the season.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: moderate deficiency — deficiency was observed across the field, without concentrated zones being reported.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3 (Representative stage: V4-V5)
  Type: Defoliation
  Species status:
    Defoliation: Unresolved (still present at the final mission), Critical window: within R1–R3 (canopy loss during flowering and pod set)
  Description: Defoliation was first detected at Mission 3 (V4-V5) at 0.3% detections in the field, remained at 0.3% at Mission 4 (R1), declined to 0.2% at Mission 5 (R2-R4), increased to 0.3% at Mission 6 (R5-R6). Critical window: within R1–R3 (canopy loss during flowering and pod set). Status: Unresolved (still present at the final mission). Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - 1 day(s) of frost risk (May 12) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 8–May 24; 11 days within Jun 14–Jun 26; 9 days within Jul 3–Jul 17; 9 days within Jul 27–Aug 10; 13 days within Aug 10–Aug 26, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.
summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Suboptimal emergence and persistent weed pressure at V1–V2 and R2–R4 likely had a significant impact on yield potential, despite generally well-managed diseases, nutrients, and insects.

**Season Detail:**
Weather stress may have broadly reduced establishment across the field, consistent with frost (below 35°F) on May 12.

Weed pressure was very high at V1–V2, remained very high through V4–V5, declined to moderate at R1, escalated to very high at R2–R4, and declined to moderate at R5–R6; pigweeds, common lambsquarters, and barnyard grass were dominant, with pressure widespread and only partial control achieved following 2.2 in of rain between Jun 28 and Jul 21, likely having a significant yield impact.

Downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact. Brown Stem Rot was detected once at R5–R6 (19.1% detections in the field), with conditions conducive to disease spread present during this period; Sudden Death Syndrome was also detected at R5–R6 in a single data point, but overall disease pressure was limited and likely negligible yield impact.

Defoliation was first detected at V4–V5 (0.3% detections in the field), remained at 0.3% at R1, declined to 0.2% at R2–R4, and increased to 0.3% at R5–R6, with pressure within the critical window and unresolved status, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.
Summary does not use bare "Managed" or "Unmanaged" as standalone labels — hedged forms like "likely managed," "consistent with management," "appears unmanaged," or "likely unresolved" are acceptable

Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 149,042 plants/acre (99% of target)
  Description: Stand count was 99% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Spatial distribution:
    - adequate: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V1-V2)
  Species: Pigweeds (V1-V2, V3-V4, V4-V5, V5-V6, V6-V7), Fleabane/Horseweed (V1-V2, V3-V4), Common Lambsquarters (V1-V2)
  Description: Weed pressure was very high at Mission 1 (V1-V2), declined to high at Mission 2 (V3-V4), escalated to very high at Mission 3 (V4-V5), declined to mild at Mission 4 (V5-V6), remained mild through Mission 5 (V6-V7), declined to none at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Early weed pressure suggests pre-emergence control was incomplete, but later applications effectively reduced competition. Post-emergence timing needs review, given moderate or higher weed pressure detected after Mission 2.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: very high pressure early, none pressure late — Early-season weed pressure was widespread across the field, and early weed pressure suggests pre-emergence control was incomplete, but later applications effectively reduced competition.
  Yield impact: yes — some competitive drag on yield is plausible but not confirmed significant.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (V5-V6)
  Type: Brown Spot
  Non-impact detections: Downy mildew (Soybean): detected at V5-V6, Disease - Other: detected at R2-R4
  Description: Brown Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 4 (V5-V6), 24.3% detections in the field; still detected in-field at the final mission (Mission 6/6, 5.8%). Conditions between Apr 22 and May 26 were also conducive to disease spread.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — Disease detections were concentrated in localized pockets across the field, concentrated in about 11.9% of the total area.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  Type: none
  Description: No nutrient deficiencies were detected at any point during the season.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: moderate deficiency — deficiency was observed across the field, without concentrated zones being reported.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 2 (Representative stage: V3-V4)
  Type: Defoliation
  Species status:
    Defoliation: Unresolved (still present at the final mission), Critical window: within R1–R3 (canopy loss during flowering and pod set)
  Description: Defoliation was first detected at Mission 2 (V3-V4) at 0.2% detections in the field, increased to 0.5% at Mission 3 (V4-V5), declined to 0.4% at Mission 4 (V5-V6), declined to 0.3% at Mission 5 (V6-V7), remained at 0.3% at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Critical window: within R1–R3 (canopy loss during flowering and pod set). Status: Unresolved (still present at the final mission). Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Heavy precipitation events (May 24 (2.0 in)) between planting and Mission 1 likely contributed to soil compaction and emergence challenges.
  - 8 day(s) of frost risk (Apr 24–May 20) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 13 days within Apr 25–May 22; 6 days within Jun 21–Jul 2; 5 days within Jul 10–Jul 24; 8 days within Jul 30–Aug 12, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Mild weed pressure at V5–V6, V6–V7, and R2–R4 and unresolved Brown Spot during grain fill likely had a moderate impact on yield potential, despite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 99% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was very high at V1–V2, declined to high at V3–V4, escalated to very high at V4–5, then declined to mild at V5–V6 and was no longer detected by R2–R4; pigweeds, fleabane/horseweed, and common lambsquarters were dominant, with early pressure suggesting pre-emergence control was incomplete and later applications reducing competition — likely having a moderate yield impact.

Downy mildew was detected but is considered low impact. Brown Spot was first detected at V5–V6 (24.3% detections in the field), declining to 5.8% at R2–R4 and was still present at the final assessment; conditions lent themselves to disease pressure during this period, but overall impact was likely negligible.

Defoliation was first detected at V3–V4 (0.2% detections in the field), increased to 0.5% at V4–V5, declined to 0.3% at V6–V7 and remained at this low level through R2–R4, with pressure within the critical window and likely negligible yield impact.

No nutrient deficiencies were detected at any point during the season, likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Persistent sulfur deficiency likely had a significant impact on yield potential, despite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 93% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was absent at VE, escalated to mild at V3–V4, was controlled by V6–V12, and returned to mild at R2–R4, with pressure remaining low throughout the season; likely negligible yield impact.

High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 7 days within Apr 25–May 1; 6 days within May 17–May 22; 7 days within Jun 7–Jun 25; 6 days within Jun 25–Jul 11; 8 days within Jul 11–Jul 24, coinciding with in-field disease detections. No impact diseases were detected in-field across the season, and the canopy remained fully intact; Gray Leaf Spot was present in up to 10 fields regionally but not detected in this field, NCLB and Tar Spot were each detected regionally in up to 4 and 1 field, respectively, by R2–R4 — likely negligible yield impact.

Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V13–V16 (76.8% detections in the field), appearing following 4.4 in of rain between Jun 6 and Jun 25, with leaching a likely contributing factor, likely having a significant yield impact.

Stink bug, chewing damage, and other low-impact insect activity were detected at low levels, with stink bug not detected by the final mission and overall insect pressure remaining low, likely negligible yield impact.

**Season Conclusion:**
Weed pressure at V1–V2 and elevated insect pressure at V13–V16 likely had a moderate impact on yield potential, despite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 93% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was very high at V1–V2, remained very high through V5–V6, declined to moderate at V6–V12, then declined to mild by V13–V16 and remained mild through the end of the season; pigweeds, common lambsquarters, and barnyard grass were dominant, with early pressure suggesting pre-emergence control was incomplete and later applications effectively reducing competition — likely having a moderate yield impact.

Holcus Leaf Spot was detected but is considered low impact. Northern Corn Leaf Blight was first detected at VT–R1 (0.4% detections in the field), peaked at 0.5%, and was still present at 0.5% at the final assessment; Gray Leaf Spot was first detected at VT–R1 and present but not significant at the final mission. Both diseases were detected regionally alongside in-field appearance, and conditions lent themselves to disease pressure during this period. Rust and Tar Spot were present regionally but not detected in this field, with likely negligible yield impact.

Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V6–V12 (12.1% detections in the field), decreasing to 1.3% by VT–R1 and no longer detected by the final mission. Deficiency - Other was detected once at V13–V16 (0.4%). Nitrogen deficiency was detected once at R2–R4 (0.9%). These deficiencies were transient or well within adequate range, likely negligible yield impact.

Stink bug and European corn borer were detected at V6–V12 and not detected by the final mission, with stink bug within the critical window R1–R3 and European corn borer at V6–V8; chewing damage was first detected at V5–V6 (0.9%), increased to 45.7% at V13–V16, and reached 70.8% at VT–R1, while grasshopper and grasshopper damage were also observed at low levels. Overall, insect pressure remained low, likely negligible yield impact.

This check owns the second half: it fails only when a sub-threshold category appears in the blame clause (before any "despite"/"although"), e.g. "recurring nutrient deficiencies likely reduced yield potential" with nutrients at 0.26 bu/ac (field 1312164). Favourable mentions such as "effective weed and insect control" are explicitly allowed -- they accounted for 38 of the 80 failing cells on the 412-field GT baseline and are not defects.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
No significant yield impact identified this season — strong emergence and in-season management kept all threats to a minor factor.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 95% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was very high at V3–V4, declined to high at V4–V5, then declined to mild at V13–V16 before being controlled by R2–R4; pressure decreased only partially following treatment, with barnyard grass and morning glory concentrated in pockets, but likely negligible yield impact.

High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 17 days within Apr 25–May 25; 8 days within Jun 8–Jun 23; 11 days within Jun 26–Jul 11; 10 days within Jul 31–Aug 18, coinciding with in-field disease detections. Holcus Leaf Spot and Downy mildew were detected but are considered low impact. No impact diseases were detected in-field, and the canopy remained fully intact; NCLB, Gray Leaf Spot, and Tar Spot were present regionally but not detected in this field, likely negligible yield impact.

Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V13–V16 (4.8% detections in the field), peaked at 47.6%, and was no longer detected by the final mission, likely negligible yield impact.

Japanese beetle was detected at VT–R1 (4.8% detections in the field) within the critical window, and chewing damage was observed at VT–R1 (14.3%), but overall insect pressure remained low, likely negligible yield impact.

failed.reasoning: Any specific named threat (species, disease, deficiency) mentioned in the summary must appear in the analysis

A weed sentence must not use resolution/control language ("controlled", "resolved", "no longer a factor", "effectively controlled") when the record's actual final-mission Pressure label is still moderate or higher, nor claim a decrease when the final mission's label never actually dropped below the season's peak. Grounded directly in season_data's per-mission Pressure labels (weed severity has no percentage to cite), not in whatever the sentence itself happens to state — closes a gap TREND_WORD_ACCURACY cannot see, since that check only catches a persistence verb contradicted by a percentage cited in the SAME sentence, never a resolution/decrease claim checked against season_data itself. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

Season Conclusion must not assert a blanket "effective management" verdict for the whole season when the CATEGORY STATUS ground truth (copied into the analysis' Status: lines) shows any category as Unresolved. "Effective" is a definitive, unhedged claim of the same kind the Trajectory Language rules already ban for bare "Managed"/"Unmanaged" — hedged forms ("apparent effective management," "likely effective management," "appears to have been effectively managed") are acceptable.

Persistent potassium and nitrogen deficiencies likely had a significant impact on yield potential, despite strong emergence.

Stand count was 96% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 17–May 22; 13 days within Jun 21–Jul 9; 7 days within Jul 11–Jul 25; 13 days within Jul 29–Aug 14, coinciding with in-field disease detections. Holcus Leaf Spot was detected but is considered low impact. No impact diseases were detected in-field across the season, and the canopy remained fully intact; Gray Leaf Spot, NCLB, Tar Spot, and Rust were present in nearby fields regionally but not detected in this field, likely negligible yield impact.

Potassium deficiency was first detected at V4–V5 (1% detections in the field), decreased to 0.8% by V13–V16, and was no longer detected by the final mission, concentrated in about 5% of the field. Sulfur deficiency was first detected at V4–V5 (1%), peaking at 60.2% and no longer detected by the final mission. Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at R2–R4 (18.6%), peaking at 28.4%, with persistent deficiency likely having a significant yield impact.

Stink bug was detected at V4–V5 (1% detections in the field), declined to 0.8% at V13–V16, and was not detected by the final mission, with critical window after R4; chewing damage was also observed at V13–V16 (4.2%) and V2–V3 (2.9%), but overall insect pressure was low and likely negligible yield impact.

summary_cases.output_text:
**Season Conclusion:**
Moderate weed pressure at V5–V6 scattered detections at VT-R1 likely had a moderate impact on yield potentialdespite strong emergence.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 97% of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was mild at V1–V2, escalated to high at V5–V6, reached very high at V6–12, then declined to mild by V13–V16 and remained mild through the end of the season. Pigweeds, velvetleaf, and fleabane/horseweed were dominant, with pressure concentrated in widespread pockets; favorable moisture following 3 in of rain between May 13 and May 29 may have supported additional weed germination, likely having a moderate yield impact.

Northern Corn Leaf Blight was first detected at VT-R1 (0.6% detections in the field), with no longer detected by the final mission; NCLB, Gray Leaf Spot, Tar Spot, and Rust were all detected regionally alongside in-field detection, but were not present in this field. Weather conditions were conducive to disease spread during this period. Holcus Leaf Spot was detected but is considered low impact. NCLB pressure was limited and likely negligible yield impact.

Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at VT-R1 (0.6% detections in the field), concentrated in about 3% of the field, likely negligible yield impact.

Chewing damage was detected at VT-R1 (9.3% detections in the field), but overall insect pressure remained low and likely negligible yield impact.
