failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 29,868 plants/acre (93% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 93% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Spatial distribution:
    - adequate: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V1-V2)
  Species: Pigweeds (V4-V5, V6-V12, V13-V16), Volunteer soybean (V1-V2), Volunteer corn (V1-V2)
  Description: Weed pressure was mild at Mission 1 (V1-V2), remained mild through Mission 2 (V4-V5), remained mild through Mission 3 (V6-V12), remained mild through Mission 4 (V13-V16), declined to none at Mission 5 (R2-R4), remained none through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Spatial distribution:
    - none pressure: mild pressure early, none pressure late — Weed pressure was observed across the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  First detected: Not detected in-field
  Type: None detected in-field
  Regional context: Tar Spot, and Gray Leaf Spot were detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but were not detected in this field.
  Description: No impact diseases were detected in-field across any late-season flight. Despite regional detections of Tar Spot, and Gray Leaf Spot in nearby fields during the R2-R4 window, your field remained free of these diseases, and the canopy stayed fully intact all season.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: low pressure — no impact diseases detected across the field.
  Yield impact: no — canopy integrity was maintained throughout the season.

Nutrients — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → Middle Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V13-V16)
  Type: Sulfur, Nitrogen
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was detected once, at Mission 4, with 24.7% detections in the field at V13-V16. Nitrogen deficiency was detected once, at Mission 5, with 2.5% at R2-R4.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 6% of the field.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  First detected: Mission 3 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Type: Chewing Damage, Chewing
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 1.3% at V6-V12
  - Chewing: 3.7% at R2-R4
  Description: Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 3 (V6-V12) at 1.3% detections in the field. Chewing was first detected at Mission 6 (R2-R4) at 3.7%. Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - 2 day(s) of frost risk (May 6–May 7) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 17–May 22; 11 days within Jun 16–Jul 1; 5 days within Jul 4–Jul 15; 8 days within Jul 23–Aug 6, but no impact diseases developed in-field.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

Consider a stronger pre-emergence residual targeting volunteer corn, cockleburs, and grass to close the gap that allowed early-season escapes.

Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 32,383 plants/acre (107% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 107% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V1-V2)
  Species: Pigweeds (V1-V2, V6-V12, VT-R1, R2-R4), Barnyard grass (V6-V12, VT-R1, R2-R4), Velvetleaf (VT-R1, R2-R4)
  Description: Weed pressure was mild at Mission 1 (V1-V2), remained mild through Mission 2 (V6-V12), remained mild through Mission 3 (V6-V12), remained mild through Mission 4 (VT-R1), remained mild through Mission 5 (R2-R4), remained mild through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: mild pressure throughout — Weed pressure was concentrated in localized pockets across the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → Middle Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3 (V6-V12)
  Type: Gray Leaf Spot, Tar Spot
  Non-impact detections: Holcus Leaf Spot: 39.4% at V6-V12, Anthracnose leaf blight: detected at V6-V12
  Description: Gray Leaf Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 3 (V6-V12), 2.8% detections in the field, peaked at 5.1%; no longer detected in-field by the final mission (Mission 6/6). Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 17 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Tar Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 5 (R2-R4), 5.2%; no longer detected in-field by the final mission (Mission 6/6). Tar Spot was also detected regionally in up to 2 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Conditions between May 5 and May 23 were also conducive to disease spread. NCLB, and Rust were detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but were not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — disease was present in scattered pockets across the field, without a single dominant zone.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Recurring / Intermittent
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Type: Sulfur, Nitrogen
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was detected once, at Mission 3, with 0.4% detections in the field at V6-V12. Nitrogen deficiency was detected once, at Mission 5, with 0.4% at R2-R4.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 2% of the field.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 2 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Type: Chewing Damage, stink bug damage, Stink Bug, Chewing
  Species status:
    Stink Bug: Managed (not detected by the final mission), Critical window: within R1–R3 (kernel feeding during set)
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 11.4% at VT-R1
  - Insect - Other: 0.4% at V6-V12
  - Chewing: 1.2% at R2-R4
  Description: Stink Bug was first detected at Mission 5 (R2-R4) at 0.4% detections in the field. Critical window: within R1–R3 (kernel feeding during set). This appears managed (not detected by the final mission). Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 2 (V6-V12) at 0.4%, remained at 0.4% at Mission 3 (V6-V12), increased to 11.4% at Mission 4 (VT-R1). stink bug damage was first detected at Mission 2 (V6-V12) at 0.8%. Chewing was first detected at Mission 6 (R2-R4) at 1.2%. Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Heavy precipitation events (May 16 (2.6 in)) between planting and Mission 1 likely contributed to soil compaction and emergence challenges.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 7 days within May 5–May 22; 5 days within May 28–Jun 8; 6 days within Jun 23–Jul 9; 5 days within Jul 15–Jul 26; 10 days within Aug 4–Aug 15, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
reco_cases.output_text:
Consider a stronger pre-emergence residual targeting pigweeds, barnyard grass, and velvetleaf to close the gap that allowed early-season escapes. Review nutrient timing, placement, and loss mitigation practices.

Continue the current disease management program.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

reco_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 32,710 plants/acre (92% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 92% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Spatial distribution:
    - adequate: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 2 (Representative stage: V1-V2)
  Species: Pigweeds (V4-V5, V13-V16, R2-R4), Barnyard grass (V4-V5, V13-V16, VT-R1), Velvetleaf (V4-V5, R2-R4)
  Description: Weed pressure was none at Mission 1 (VE-V1), escalated to mild at Mission 2 (V1-V2), remained mild through Mission 3 (V4-V5), remained mild through Mission 4 (V13-V16), remained mild through Mission 5 (VT-R1), remained mild through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition. Favorable moisture following 1.7 in of rain between May 3 and May 20 may have supported additional weed germination.
  Spatial distribution:
    - hotspots: none pressure early, mild pressure late — Weed pressure was concentrated in a single hotspot in the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 6 (R2-R4)
  Type: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight
  Non-impact detections: Holcus Leaf Spot: 0.9% at VT-R1, Downy mildew: 0.5% at VT-R1
  Description: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4), 7.7% detections in the field — a single data point, not a trajectory. Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was also detected regionally in up to 1 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, around the same time it was detected in-field. Conditions between May 3 and May 20 were also conducive to disease spread. Gray Leaf Spot, and Tar Spot were detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but were not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — Disease detections were concentrated in localized pockets across the field, concentrated in about 6.7% of the total area.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V13-V16)
  Type: Sulfur, Nitrogen
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was first detected at Mission 4, with 15.7% detections in the field at V13-V16, peaked at 17.6%, and was no longer detected by the final mission. Nitrogen deficiency was detected once, at Mission 6, with 1.4% at R2-R4.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Moderate deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 7% of the field.
  Yield impact: yes — some yield drag is plausible but not confirmed significant.

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V13-V16)
  Type: Chewing Damage
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 0.9% at V13-V16
  Description: Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 4 (V13-V16) at 0.9% detections in the field, declined to 0.5% at Mission 5 (VT-R1). Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - 3 day(s) of frost risk (May 5–May 7) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 5–May 20; 6 days within Jun 8–Jun 27; 8 days within Jun 27–Jul 10; 5 days within Jul 15–Jul 30, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.

Continue the current disease management program.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  First detected: Not detected in-field

  Regional context: NCLB, and Gray Leaf Spot were detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but were not detected in this field.
  Description: No impact diseases were detected in-field across any late-season flight. Despite regional detections of NCLB, and Gray Leaf Spot in nearby fields during the R2-R4 window, your field remained free of these diseases, and the canopy stayed fully intact all season.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: low pressure — no impact diseases detected across the field.
  Yield impact: no — canopy integrity was maintained throughout the season.

Nutrients — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V13-V16)
  Type: Sulfur deficiency
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was first detected at Mission 4, with 9.7% detections in the field at V13-V16, and decreased to 2.1% by R2-R4.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 12% of the field.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 5 (Representative stage: VT-R1)
  Type: Chewing Damage
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 15.6% at VT-R1
  - Insect - Other: 1.6% at VT-R1
  Description: Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 5 (VT-R1) at 15.6% detections in the field. Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - 2 day(s) of frost risk (May 5–May 7) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 5–May 20; 7 days within Jun 13–Jul 1; 7 days within Jul 1–Jul 16; 8 days within Jul 22–Aug 4, but no impact diseases developed in-field.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: V0-VE)

Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Spatial distribution:
    - hotspots: mild pressure early, none pressure late — Weed pressure was concentrated in a single hotspot in the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (V6-V12)
  Type: None detected in-field
  Non-impact detections: Holcus Leaf Spot: 2.1% at V6-V12
  Regional context: Gray Leaf Spot was detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but was not detected in this field.
  Description: No impact diseases were detected in-field across any late-season flight. Despite regional detections of Gray Leaf Spot in nearby fields during the R2-R4 window, your field remained free of these diseases, and the canopy stayed fully intact all season.
  Spatial distribution:
    - widespread: low pressure — no impact diseases detected across the field.
  Yield impact: no — canopy integrity was maintained throughout the season.

  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Moderate
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Type: Sulfur, Nitrogen
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was first detected at Mission 4, with 13.6% detections in the field at V6-V12, peaked at 29.1%, and decreased to 0.7% by R2-R4. Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at Mission 5, with 0.7% at VT-R1, peaked at 2%.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Moderate deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 8% of the field.
  Yield impact: yes — some yield drag is plausible but not confirmed significant.

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None
  First detected: Mission 6 (Representative stage: R2-R4)
  Type: Chewing
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing: 2.7% at R2-R4
  Description: Chewing was first detected at Mission 6 (R2-R4) at 2.7% detections in the field. Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - 4 day(s) of frost risk (May 5–May 20) in the planting-to-emergence window may have contributed to stand loss and uneven emergence.
  - 1 day(s) of frost risk (May 20) occurred during the Mission 1 → Mission 2 window.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 5–May 20; 7 days within Jun 12–Jun 28; 7 days within Jun 28–Jul 9, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.

A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

reco_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Good Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 29,707 plants/acre (98% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 98% of target. Strong emergence and establishment.
  Spatial distribution:
    - adequate: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: no — stand established well

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 2 (Representative stage: V4-V5)
  Species: Pigweeds (V4-V5, V6-V12), Barnyard grass (V4-V5, V6-V12), Velvetleaf (V1-V2)
  Description: Weed pressure was none at Mission 1 (V1-V2), escalated to mild at Mission 2 (V4-V5), remained mild through Mission 3 (V6-V12), declined to none at Mission 4 (V13-V16), remained none through Mission 5 (R2-R4), remained none through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition. Favorable moisture following 3.1 in of rain between May 10 and May 29 may have supported additional weed germination.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: none pressure throughout — Weed pressure was concentrated in localized pockets across the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 6 (R2-R4)
  Type: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight, Gray Leaf Spot
  Non-impact detections: Holcus Leaf Spot: 17% at V13-V16
  Description: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4), 16.3% detections in the field — a single data point, not a trajectory. Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight was also detected regionally in up to 12 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, before it was detected in-field. Gray Leaf Spot was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4) — a single data point, not a trajectory. Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 8 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, before it was detected in-field. Conditions between May 10 and May 29 were also conducive to disease spread.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — disease was present in scattered pockets across the field, without a single dominant zone.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Recurring / Intermittent
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Significant
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V13-V16)
  Type: Sulfur, Nitrogen
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was detected once, at Mission 4, with 50.4% detections in the field at V13-V16. Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at Mission 4, with 0.7% at V13-V16, peaked at 1.5%.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Significant deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 7% of the field.
  Yield impact: yes — persistent deficiency likely limited nutrient availability during a yield-relevant growth stage.

Insects — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Type: Chewing Damage, Chewing, Insect pressure
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 12.1% at V13-V16
  - Insect - Other: 5.7% at V13-V16
  - Chewing: 5.9% at R2-R4
  - Insect pressure: 27.4% at R2-R4
  Description: Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 3 (V6-V12) at 1.4% detections in the field, increased to 12.1% at Mission 4 (V13-V16). Chewing was first detected at Mission 5 (R2-R4) at 1.5%, increased to 5.9% at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Insect pressure was first detected at Mission 5 (R2-R4) at 0.8%, increased to 27.4% at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Heavy precipitation events (Aug 11 (2.6 in)) occurred during the Mission 5 → Mission 6 window.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within May 17–May 22; 5 days within Jun 14–Jun 21; 8 days within Jun 23–Jul 4; 6 days within Jul 11–Jul 25; 12 days within Jul 29–Aug 14, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
  - No drought or heat stress flags were present during the late-season reproductive windows, so water availability was not a limiting factor during reproductive stages.
reco_cases.output_text:
Consider a stronger pre-emergence residual targeting pigweeds, barnyard grass, and velvetleaf to close the gap that allowed early-season escapes. Review nutrient timing, placement, and loss mitigation practices.

Continue the current disease management program.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

reco_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Medium Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 22,148 plants/acre (79% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 79% of target. Suboptimal but uniform emergence. Since weather conditions were generally favorable, non-weather factors may have contributed to the reduced stand.
  Spatial distribution:
    - below threshold: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: yes — sub-optimal emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season. Emergence occurred at 157 GDD, later than typical for VE.

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: VE)
  Species: Barnyard grass (VE-V1, V6-V12, R2-R4)
  Description: Weed pressure was mild at Mission 1 (VE), remained mild through Mission 2 (VE-V1), remained mild through Mission 3 (V4-V5), remained mild through Mission 4 (V6-V12), remained mild through Mission 5 (R2-R4), remained mild through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition. Reduced crop establishment may have increased crop-weed competition.
  Spatial distribution:
    - hotspots: mild pressure throughout — Weed pressure was concentrated in a single hotspot in the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 6 (R2-R4)
  Type: Gray Leaf Spot
  Non-impact detections: Holcus Leaf Spot: 53.8% at R2-R4
  Description: Gray Leaf Spot was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4), 3.5% detections in the field — a single data point, not a trajectory. Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 8 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, before it was detected in-field. Conditions between May 3 and May 19 were also conducive to disease spread. NCLB was detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but was not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — Disease detections were concentrated in localized pockets across the field, concentrated in about 15% of the total area.
  Yield impact: no — disease pressure was limited and canopy function was largely maintained.

Nutrients — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V6-V12)
  Type: Sulfur deficiency
  Description: Sulfur deficiency was first detected at Mission 4, with 5.4% detections in the field at V6-V12, peaked at 7.5%, and decreased to 2.3% by R2-R4, and appeared following heavy rainfall (7.7 in between Jun 15 and Jul 5), suggesting nutrient leaching may have contributed to the observed deficiency.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 7% of the field.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Recurring / Intermittent
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3 (Representative stage: V4-V5)
  Type: Chewing Damage, stink bug damage, Chewing, Stink Bug, Insect pressure
  Species status:
    Stink Bug: Unresolved (still present at the final mission), Critical window: within R1–R3 (kernel feeding during set)
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 11.8% at V6-V12
  - Insect - Other: 4.3% at V6-V12
  - Chewing: 18.4% at R2-R4
  - Insect pressure: 1.1% at R2-R4
  Description: Stink Bug was first detected at Mission 5 (R2-R4) at 1.1% detections in the field, remained at 1.1% at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Critical window: within R1–R3 (kernel feeding during set). Status: Unresolved (still present at the final mission). Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 3 (V4-V5) at 1%, increased to 11.8% at Mission 4 (V6-V12). stink bug damage was first detected at Mission 4 (V6-V12) at 1.1%. Chewing was first detected at Mission 5 (R2-R4) at 2.1%, increased to 18.4% at Mission 6 (R2-R4). Insect pressure was first detected at Mission 6 (R2-R4) at 1.1%. Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Multiple heavy precipitation events (Jun 20 (2.1 in)) during the Mission 3 → Mission 4 window increased the risk of nutrient leaching and delivery challenges, particularly for Sulfur.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 6 days within May 5–May 19; 6 days within Jun 21–Jun 27, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
reco_cases.output_text:
Consider redesigning the weed management program with a stronger pre-emergence residual targeting barnyard grass and broadleaf species to close the gap that allowed early-season escapes.

Be ready to spray a fungicide targeting Gray Leaf Spot at the early reproductive stages if in-field and regional foliar disease pressure are similar to this season. Crop rotation and debris management reduce the risk of Gray Leaf Spot next year by minimizing overwintering fungus.

Review nutrient timing, placement, and loss mitigation practices — consider splitting your application to reduce the risk of sulfur leaching in case of heavy rainfall next season.

Consider a targeted response to stink bug at the R1–R3 window next season if pressure develops — monitor for stink bug presence beginning at early reproductive stages.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

reco_cases.season_analysis_text:
Emergence — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Medium Emergence
  Stand count (latest early-season reading): 14,286 plants/acre (85% of target)
  Phenological state: uniform
  Description: Stand count was 85% of target. Suboptimal but uniform emergence. Since weather conditions were generally favorable, non-weather factors may have contributed to the reduced stand.
  Spatial distribution:
    - below threshold: Stand count was consistent across the field, with no distinctive low or high stand count regions detected.
  Yield impact: yes — sub-optimal emergence set a lower yield ceiling for the season.

Weeds — Season Priority: Low
  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 1 (Representative stage: VE)
  Species: Pigweeds (V1-V2, R2-R4), Fleabane/Horseweed (VE, V1-V2), Morning glory (V1-V2)
  Description: Weed pressure was mild at Mission 1 (VE), remained mild through Mission 2 (V1-V2), remained mild through Mission 3 (V5-V6), remained mild through Mission 4 (V13-V16), remained mild through Mission 5 (R2-R4), remained mild through Mission 6 (R2-R4). Weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition. Reduced crop establishment may have increased crop-weed competition.
  Spatial distribution:
    - hotspots: mild pressure throughout — Weed pressure was concentrated in a single hotspot in the field, and weed pressure remained low throughout the season, suggesting effective weed control and limited crop competition.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Diseases — Season Priority: High
  Scenario: Start Absent/Low → End Med/High
  Status: Unresolved
  Materiality: Significant
  First detected: Mission 5 (R2-R4)
  Type: Gray Leaf Spot, Tar Spot
  Non-impact detections: Holcus Leaf Spot: 91.7% at V5-V6
  Description: Gray Leaf Spot was first detected in-field at Mission 5 (R2-R4), 0.7% detections in the field; present in-field but not significant at the final mission (Mission 6/6). Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 8 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, before it was detected in-field. Tar Spot was detected once, at Mission 6 (R2-R4), 19.2% — a single data point, not a trajectory. Conditions between Jun 18 and Jul 8 were also conducive to disease spread. NCLB was detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but was not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Significant pressure — Disease detections were concentrated in localized pockets across the field, concentrated in about 7.6% of the total area.
  Yield impact: yes — unresolved in-field disease pressure likely reduced canopy function during a yield-relevant window.

Nutrients — Season Priority: Moderate
  Scenario: Start Med/High → End Absent/Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 3 (Representative stage: V5-V6)
  Type: Potassium, Sulfur
  Description: Potassium deficiency was first detected at Mission 3, with 0.7% detections in the field at V5-V6, concentrated in about 4% of the field. Sulfur deficiency was first detected at Mission 4, with 2.3% at V13-V16, peaked at 4.3%, and appeared following heavy rainfall (7.1 in between Jun 18 and Jul 8), suggesting nutrient leaching may have contributed to the observed deficiency, and was no longer detected by the final mission.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible deficiency — Deficiency was concentrated in about 9% of the field.
  Yield impact: no — deficiency was transient or well within adequate range.

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: Negligible
  First detected: Mission 4 (Representative stage: V13-V16)
  Type: Chewing Damage
  Low-impact detections:
  - Chewing damage: 6.8% at V13-V16
  Description: Chewing Damage was first detected at Mission 4 (V13-V16) at 6.8% detections in the field. Overall, insect pressure remained low throughout the season, with no material impact on crop development.
  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Multiple heavy precipitation events (Jun 20 (2.9 in)) during the Mission 3 → Mission 4 window increased the risk of nutrient leaching and delivery challenges, particularly for Sulfur.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 5 days within Jun 21–Jun 26, coinciding with in-field disease detections.
reco_cases.output_text:
Consider redesigning the weed management program with a stronger pre-emergence residual targeting pigweeds, fleabane/horseweed, and morning glory to close the gap that allowed early-season escapes.

Be ready to spray a fungicide targeting Gray Leaf Spot and Tar Spot prior to VT if in-field and regional foliar disease pressure are similar to this season. Gray Leaf Spot was present in-field but not significant at the final mission, with regional detections preceding in-field appearance. Tar Spot was detected at the final mission, and NCLB was present regionally but not detected in this field. Crop rotation and debris management reduce the risk of Gray Leaf Spot and Tar Spot next year by minimizing overwintering fungus.

Review nutrient timing, placement, and loss mitigation practices — consider splitting your application to reduce the risk of Sulfur leaching in case of heavy rainfall next season.

Continue the current insect management program.

failed.reasoning: Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

  Yield impact: no — pressure was low or well controlled with limited yield risk.

  Scenario: Steady Low
  Status: Managed
  Materiality: Negligible

  Type: Northern (Tercicum) corn leaf blight, Gray Leaf Spot

Gray Leaf Spot was also detected regionally in up to 47 field(s) within a 20-mile radius, before it was detected in-field. Conditions between May 13 and Jun 3 were also conducive to disease spread. Tar Spot, and Rust were detected in fields within a 20-mile radius during the late season, but were not detected in this field.
  Spatial distribution:
    - pockets: Negligible pressure — disease was present in scattered pockets across the field, without a single dominant zone.

  Spatial distribution:
    - scattered: Negligible deficiency — Sulfur deficiencies are scattered around the field, not concentrated in any particular region(s).

Insects — Season Priority: No Threat
  Scenario: Steady Absent
  Status: No Threat
  Materiality: None

  Type: Chewing
  Low-impact detections:

  Yield impact: no — pressure was low-impact or well controlled with limited yield risk.

Weather Context
  Conditions that likely shaped yield outcomes:
  - Heavy precipitation events (Jul 9 (2.2 in)) occurred during the Mission 3 → Mission 4 window.
  - High humidity conducive to disease spread was present for 7 days within May 14–May 27; 6 days within Jun 7–Jun 23; 5 days within Jun 23–Jun 29; 7 days within Jul 5–Jul 21; 6 days within Jul 28–Aug 9; 7 days within Aug 16–Aug 27, coinciding with in-field disease detections.

A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

Wording may vary but the qualifier word must match the category's Materiality; do not re-derive the qualifier from severity language. Binary: a summary that omits one category's phrase is not partly right about that category, and proportional credit would score it above CORRECTION_THRESHOLD where no correction can reach it.

Sibling of SEASON_SUMMARY_CONCLUSION_YIELD_IMPACT_COVERAGE, split out 2026-08-18. The Season Conclusion inclusion rule is asymmetric: a category at or above the crop Final_Yield_Impact threshold (corn 5 bu/ac, soy 3) must be named AS A CAUSE, while a category below the threshold may be named only favourably -- credited as controlled or as having no material impact. This check owns the second half: it fails only when a sub-threshold category appears in the blame clause (before any "despite"/"although"), e.g. "recurring nutrient deficiencies likely reduced yield potential" with nutrients at 0.26 bu/ac (field 1312164). Favourable mentions such as "effective weed and insect control" are explicitly allowed -- they accounted for 38 of the 80 failing cells on the 412-field GT baseline and are not defects.

Per-element, not per-category — a category-level Unresolved status can coexist with one specific nutrient genuinely having resolved. Flagged critical=True in the subscriber repo.

C1-ext-a: a weed control-achieved claim ("controlled by X", "declined to mild by X") must name a stage whose mission was actually at or below the controlled (mild/none) Pressure label, and pressure must not exceed that level again afterwards. Scoped to the banned-phrasing rule in the doc; the stronger reviewer "must name the EARLIEST controlled mission" reading is deliberately NOT implemented -- it fired on 58/412 GT fields, almost all correct prose, and has no doc basis.

v2 of SEASON_SUMMARY_INSECT_STAGE_ATTRIBUTION, run side by side for comparison before v1 is retired (added 2026-08-15 after v1 was found to be 7/10 false positives on a live SA batch). Same rule, but: matches "detected" + stage token within the same clause only, not anywhere later in the sentence (compound sentences naming multiple insects were letting one insect's bare "detected" borrow a different, later insect's own stage citation); skips any clause with a negated "detected" ("not detected", "went undetected") rather than reading it as a positive claim; and resolves insect mentions through an alias map so a narrative eliding season_data's generic suffix ("stink bug" for "stink bug damage") still resolves correctly instead of falling back to an unrelated nearby insect name. A claim that cites an accurate 0%/absent value at one endpoint of a season-long range (e.g. "ranging from 0.0% at V1-V2 to 0.7% at R2-R4") is still flagged -- that framing is what this check exists to catch, not a matching bug.

Every weather-event sentence must contain an exact date/duration — vague forms like "early frost" or "heavy rain" without a date fail (score 0). A quantitative measure (inches, °F) is additionally required for primary yield-explaining clauses; secondary disease-context sentences that have a date but no quantity score 5. Rain or precipitation must always include an amount in inches — "heavy rain" or "significant precipitation" without a quantity fails even if a date is present. If multiple rain events are cited together, the sum must be stated. Generic window labels (e.g., "planting window," "planting-to-emergence window") must not be used as a timeframe for a cited rainfall figure — a specific date range or sub-window (e.g., "in the 48 hours after planting," "May 5–6") is required; using a generic label scores 0. Discrete rain events separated by dry days must be cited individually — compressing them into a continuous range (e.g., "Jun 10–Jun 15" when events were Jun 10 and Jun 14 with dry days between) scores 0.

Weed recommendation must not call for a "more robust" or strengthened pre-emergence program when the pre-emergence program was working: early-season weed pressure (M1–M2) was none, or was mild and did not increase after M2. A late-season escalation off NONE early pressure is a post-emergence problem — the recommendation must address post-emergence timing, not pre-emergence strengthening. Mild early pressure that then increased after M2 DOES require strengthening — critical: failing this hides all results and blocks the result-created event

Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS) and Brown Stem Rot (BSR) are soil-borne/vascular diseases — a foliar fungicide application does not control them. They must never be named in the "be ready to spray a fungicide..." readiness sentence or the "...management was effective — continue the current fungicide program" managed sentence, regardless of their Status. They remain impact diseases for analysis/summary/Season Conclusion purposes — this rule applies to the recommendation only.

Inverse of N4 (SEASON_RECO_EMERGENCE_PLANTER_CALIBRATION): a planting-equipment clause (planter calibration, singulation, seeding depth, seed spacing) must itself be grounded in a real emergence-variability signal — a sub-optimal, corn emergence scenario carrying a variability flag in season_data. A recommendation that reaches for this clause off a good/optimal stand, off soy, or with no variability flag at all is unsupported.
